title: The periodic tensor calculation for a square-zero exact divisor
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $t\in R$ satisfy $t^2=0$ and $\{r\in R:tr=0\}=tR$. Put $F=R/tR$. The augmented sequence $\cdots\xrightarrow{t}R\xrightarrow{t}R\to F\to0$ is a free resolution, and for every $q\geq0$ one has $H^{-q}(F\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}F)\cong F$, equivalently $\operatorname{Tor}^R_q(F,F)\cong F$. Here derived tensor is computed from K-flat resolutions [def-pc-kflat-complex] in the derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For every scheme $V$, let $R_V,F_V$ denote constant sheaves on $V_{\mathrm{proét}}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Then $H^{-q}(F_V\otimes_{R_V}^{\mathbf L}F_V)\cong F_V$ for every $q\geq0$, with derived tensor as in [def-weil-derived-tensor]. If $F\ne0$ and $V$ is nonempty, all these sheaves are nonzero.

source.place: The examples, periodic multiplication resolution; generalized from Z/ell^2 to an exact square-zero divisor

proof.text: Define $P^i=R$ for $i\leq0$, $P^i=0$ for $i>0$, and $d^i=t\cdot-$ for $i<0$, with all other differentials zero. Augment $P^0$ by the quotient map $\pi:R\to F$. The equations $t^2=0$ and $\pi(tR)=0$ make this an augmented complex. At every negative degree its kernel and incoming image are both $tR$, by the annihilator hypothesis. At degree zero, $\ker\pi=tR$ is the incoming image and $\pi$ is surjective. Thus the augmented sequence is exact, each nonzero term is free of rank one, and $P\to F[0]$ is a quasi-isomorphism: $H^0(P)=R/tR$ and all other cohomology vanishes.

source.place: The examples: the periodic multiplication resolution, with t in place of ell

proof.text: The maps $R\otimes_R M\to M$, $r\otimes m\mapsto rm$, and $m\mapsto1\otimes m$ are inverse, since $r\otimes m=1\otimes rm$; hence $R$ is flat and the zero module is flat. The complex $P$ is bounded above by zero, so [lem-pc-module-bounded-flat-kflat] makes it K-flat. Regard $R$ as a sheaf of rings on the one-point site, so that K-flatness is that of [def-pc-kflat-complex], as in the statement. By [lem-pc-derived-tensor-second-factor-functor] (2), applied to the identity ring map $R\to R$ and $N=F[0]$, for every K-flat resolution of $F$, in particular $P\to F[0]$, the canonical map identifies $F\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}F$ with $\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes_RF[0])$ in $D(R)$, canonically and independently of the K-flat resolution chosen. Since $F[0]$ has only its degree-zero term, the total tensor has $R\otimes_R F\cong F$ in every degree $i\leq0$, zero in positive degrees, and differential $\bar x\mapsto t\bar x=0$. There is only one nonzero summand in each total degree; no convergence or interchange of infinite sums is needed.

source.place: Tag 064K, lemma-derived-tor-quasi-isomorphism; computation following the periodic resolution in the blueprint

proof.text: For the zero-differential complex just obtained, in degree $-q$ the kernel is $F$ and the incoming image is zero, for every $q\geq0$, including $q=0$ where the outgoing target is zero. Thus $H^{-q}(F\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}F)\cong F$. Here $\operatorname{Tor}^R_q(F,F)$ is the degree-$q$ homology of a free resolution of the first $F$ tensored with the second $F$; reindexing this resolution by $i=-q$ gives the same calculation.

source.place: The examples: Tor in every nonnegative degree

proof.text: Let $V$ be any scheme and take its small pro-etale site with the size convention of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Apply the constant module sheaf functor to the augmented complex of step 1, term by term. Its terms are $R_V$ in degrees at most zero, its differentials are multiplication by the constant section $t$, and its augmentation is the constant quotient map to $F_V$. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-constant-exact], this functor preserves kernels and cokernels, hence images (as kernels of cokernels). It therefore preserves each equality of incoming image and outgoing kernel from step 1. Consequently $P_V\to F_V[0]$ is a quasi-isomorphism. This uses exactness on sheaves, and imposes no Noetherian, finite-coefficient or connectedness hypothesis.

source.place: Tag 093J, lemma-constant-exact; constant sheaves of modules in section-constant

proof.text: For any $R_V$-module sheaf $M$, the sectionwise maps $R_V(U)\otimes_{R_V(U)}M(U)\to M(U)$, $a\otimes m\mapsto am$, have inverse $m\mapsto1\otimes m$ and commute with restrictions. Sheafifying gives $R_V\otimes_{R_V}M\cong M$ by [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Thus tensoring with $R_V$ is the identity functor up to this natural isomorphism and is exact; $R_V$ is flat by [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules], and the zero sheaf is flat for the same reason with the zero functor. Hence every term of $P_V$ is flat.

source.place: Tag 03ER, definition-flat, and the unit tensor maps written explicitly

proof.text: The complex $P_V$ is zero in positive degrees and termwise flat by step 5, so [lem-pc-bounded-above-flat-kflat-site] applies to $(V_{\mathrm{proet}},R_V)$ and makes it K-flat. By [def-weil-derived-tensor], $F_V\otimes_{R_V}^{\mathbf L}F_V$ is $P'\otimes_{R_V}F_V[0]$ for the chosen K-flat resolution $P'\to F_V[0]$; by [lem-weil-derived-tensor-resolution-independent], applied to $P'$ and $P_V\to F_V[0]$, it is canonically isomorphic in $D(V_{\mathrm{proet}},R)$ to $P_V\otimes_{R_V}F_V[0]$, which therefore represents it. The total tensor definition gives one term $R_V\otimes_{R_V}F_V\cong F_V$ in each nonpositive degree. Under the unit isomorphism of step 5, its differential is multiplication by $t$, which is zero: the linear map $F\to F$, $\bar x\mapsto t\bar x$, is zero and its constant sheaf map is zero. Its cohomology in degree $-q$ is therefore $\ker(0)/\operatorname{im}(0)=F_V$ for every $q\geq0$.

source.place: Tag 06YQ, lemma-bounded-flat-K-flat, and section-flat derived tensor construction

proof.text: Suppose $F\ne0$ and $V$ is nonempty. Choose $0\ne a\in F$. If the constant section $a$ mapped to zero in $F_V(V)$, local injectivity of the constant module unit [lem-sf-constant-module-unit-locally-bijective] would give a covering of $V$ on which the two constant presheaf sections $a$ and $0$ coincide. A pro-etale covering is jointly surjective on underlying points by [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], so at least one member is nonempty. On it the constant presheaf restriction is the identity of $F$, forcing $a=0$, a contradiction. Thus $F_V$ is nonzero, and step 6 makes every displayed cohomology sheaf nonzero. When $V$ is empty no nonvanishing is claimed.
